title: GA-SRMC vs SRMC on anisotropic Gaussian targets
setting: The target is a zero-mean Gaussian N(0, Sigma) with diagonal Sigma whose eigenvalues are log-spaced from 1 to kappa, sampled by a Metropolis-adjusted Langevin chain. Each arm adds a score-repellent tilt, either Euclidean (SRMC) or Fisher-weighted (GA-SRMC), with the repulsion strength alpha chosen from the same grid on separate pilot chains, and the base proposal is either plain MALA or preconditioned by the online inverse Fisher estimate. The metric is log10 of the minimum-coordinate effective sample size per post-burn-in iteration over 2000 evaluation iterations (300 burn-in), and the run also reports posterior-mean squared error relative to the true mean of zero.

paper.title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
paper.claim: Replacing the Euclidean score alignment with the trace-normalized inverse Fisher matrix M = S^{-1} gives higher effective sample size than the best scalar-alpha SRMC on anisotropic Gaussian targets, and the advantage grows with the condition number.

metric.name: log10_min_ess_per_iter
metric.description: log10 of the minimum-coordinate ESS divided by 2000 post-burn-in iterations, with ESS from autocorrelations truncated at the first negative lag. A min_effect of 0.1 is about a 26% ESS gain. Diagnostics: min_ess_per_iter (linear scale), mean_sq_err (posterior-mean squared error relative to the true mean, averaged over coordinates), accept_rate, and alpha (chosen on pilot chains).

factors.name: method
factors.description: SRMC tilts with the Euclidean alignment theta^T s(x), which corresponds to M = I. GA-SRMC uses M = trace-normalized inverse of the online Fisher estimate, so tr(S_hat M) = d. Both choose alpha from the same grid on pilot chains with equal budget.

factors.name: condition_number
factors.description: Condition number kappa of the target covariance. Eigenvalues are log-spaced from 1 to kappa, so larger values make the landscape more anisotropic.

factors.name: dimension
factors.description: Target dimension d. Larger d makes the online Fisher estimate noisier relative to a fixed 2000-iteration budget.

factors.name: base_sampler
factors.description: Base proposal. MALA uses isotropic proposal noise. FisherMALA preconditions the proposal with the online inverse Fisher estimate, so the repulsion-side matrix M is tested on top of a preconditioned sampler.
